name: timely-frontier-input
instr:
Please add frontier-driven interactive input so callers can feed partially ordered data without managing capability objects. The input owns an antichain of times it may still send at, starting at `T::minimum()`, and accepts explicit message stamps.

Expose `timely::dataflow::operators::core::input::FrontierHandle<T: Timestamp, CB: ContainerBuilder<Container: Clone>>`. Its methods are `FrontierHandle::new_with_builder() -> Self`, `FrontierHandle::frontier(&self) -> &Antichain<T>`, `FrontierHandle::to_stream<'scope>(&mut self, scope: Scope<'scope, T>) -> Stream<'scope, T, CB::Container>`, `FrontierHandle::advance_to(&mut self, next: Antichain<T>) -> Result<(), DowngradeError>`, `FrontierHandle::send<D>(&mut self, stamp: &Stamp<T>, data: D) -> Result<(), DowngradeError> where CB: PushInto<D>`, `FrontierHandle::send_batch(&mut self, stamp: &Stamp<T>, batch: &mut CB::Container) -> Result<(), DowngradeError>`, `FrontierHandle::flush(&mut self)`, and `FrontierHandle::close(self)`. For `CB = CapacityContainerBuilder<C>` with `C: Container + Clone`, provide `FrontierHandle::new() -> Self`. Use the existing `DowngradeError` type.

Advancement replaces the frontier and must be monotone in timely's partial order. A send is allowed only when every stamp element is greater than or equal to some current frontier element; an empty stamp is always allowed, even with an empty frontier. Forward the supplied stamp as a multiset without minimizing it. Rejected operations return `Err` without chan
